summary: Preinstall dropper downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall='node setup.mjs'. On npm install, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a shipped 727 KB single-line string-array-rotation obfuscated file math_init.js (WV8StW rotator over a large mixed table n7gIxM, decoder hc1jfK9 with a custom alphabet). The package advertises itself as a micro-frontend utility library with empty dependencies and an empty description; the preinstall has no relation to any documented build tooling and its only effect is to fetch an alternate language runtime and hand it an obfuscated payload to execute on the installer's machine. This is the canonical alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-based scanners. Package metadata (name @servicetitan/microfront-utils, repository pointing at github.com/servicetitan/playground.git) is consistent with impersonation of the ServiceTitan npm scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
